chapters.title: Vashti Refuses the King
chapters.html:
Esther 1

The King's Feasts

1And it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus, the Ahasuerus who reigned from India to Cush over a hundred and twenty-seven provinces,

2in those days, when King Ahasuerus sat on the throne of his kingdom in Susa the citadel,

3in the third year of his reign he gave a feast for all his officials and servants. The army of Persia and Media, the nobles and the officials of the provinces were before him,

4while he showed the riches of his royal glory and the splendor and pomp of his greatness for many days, a hundred and eighty days.

5When these days were completed, the king gave a feast of seven days for all the people who were present in Susa the citadel, from the greatest to the least, in the court of the garden of the king's palace.

6There were hangings of white cotton and blue, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and pillars of marble, and couches of gold and silver on a pavement of porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl and colored stone.

7Drink was served in vessels of gold, each vessel different from the others, and the royal wine was plentiful, as befitted the king's bounty.

8The drinking was by the rule: no one was compelled. For so the king had ordered every officer of his house, to do as each man wished.

9Queen Vashti also gave a feast for the women in the royal house that belonged to King Ahasuerus.

Vashti's Refusal

10On the seventh day, when the king's heart was merry with wine, he told Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha and Abagtha, Zethar and Carkas, the seven eunuchs who served before King Ahasuerus,

11to bring Queen Vashti before the king wearing the royal crown, to show the peoples and the officials her beauty, for she was lovely to look at.

12But Queen Vashti refused to come at the king's word sent by the eunuchs. The king was very angry, and his wrath burned within him.

13Then the king said to the wise men who knew the times, for this was the king's way before all who knew law and judgment,

14those next to him being Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena and Memucan, the seven officials of Persia and Media who saw the king's face and sat first in the kingdom:

15"According to the law, what is to be done to Queen Vashti, because she has not done the command of King Ahasuerus sent by the eunuchs?"

The Decree for Every House

16Memucan said before the king and the officials, "Queen Vashti has done wrong not against the king alone, but against all the officials and all the peoples in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus.

17For the queen's deed will go out to all the women, making their husbands contemptible in their eyes, when they say, 'King Ahasuerus ordered Queen Vashti brought before him, and she did not come.'

18This very day the noble ladies of Persia and Media who have heard of the queen's deed will say the same to all the king's officials, and there will be contempt and wrath in plenty.

19If it pleases the king, let a royal word go out from him, and let it be written among the laws of Persia and Media so that it may not pass away: that Vashti is never again to come before King Ahasuerus. Let the king give her royal position to another who is better than she.

20When the king's decree that he makes is heard throughout all his kingdom, vast as it is, all the women will give honor to their husbands, from the greatest to the least."

21The advice pleased the king and the officials, and the king did as Memucan said.

22He sent letters to all the king's provinces, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language, that every man should be master in his own house and speak the language of his people.

Notes

  • The text of Esther — rendered from the Hebrew, with Swete's Greek as witness. The Greek tells the story at greater length: it calls the king Artaxerxes, opens with a dream of Mordecai before this verse, and carries six passages that the Hebrew does not have. The English numbering gathers those at the end of the book, as chapters 11–16; the dream is 11:2–12:6. The Hebrew of Esther does not name God.

  • v1 "from India to Cush" — me-Hoddu ve-ad Kush, the far east and the far south of the empire, the Indus and the upper Nile. The same king and the same hundred and twenty-seven provinces are named again when his letters go out (8:9).

  • v6 "porphyry, marble, mother-of-pearl and colored stone" — bahat, shesh, dar, socheret, four stones of the floor. Shesh is marble; the other three occur only here, and the stones they name are uncertain.

  • v10 "when the king's heart was merry with wine" — ke-tov lev ha-melekh ba-yayin, the words used of Nabal at his feast, Nabal's heart was merry within him, for he was very drunk (1 Samuel 25:36), and of Amnon, when Amnon's heart is merry with wine (2 Samuel 13:28).

  • v13 "the wise men who knew the times" — yod'ei ha-ittim. A like phrase, yod'ei vinah la-ittim, is used of the men of Issachar who came to David, who had understanding of the times, to know what Israel ought to do (1 Chronicles 12:32).

  • v16 "Memucan" — the read form, Memukhan, as in vv14 and 21. What is written here is Momukhan.

  • v19 "so that it may not pass away" — ve-lo ya'avor, the law of Persia and Media that cannot be undone. Daniel's enemies use it: according to the law of the Medes and the Persians, which cannot be revoked (Daniel 6:8). The book turns on it: a letter sealed with the king's ring may not be revoked (8:8).

  • v22 "that every man should be master in his own house" — sorer, the verb of sar, official, the word for the king's officials throughout the chapter. The Greek has so that they would be feared in their houses.

chapters.title: Esther Made Queen
chapters.html:
Esther 2

The Search for a Queen

1After these things, when the wrath of King Ahasuerus had died down, he remembered Vashti and what she had done and what had been decreed against her.

2Then the king's young men who served him said, "Let young virgins, lovely to look at, be sought for the king.

3Let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, and let them gather every young virgin lovely to look at to Susa the citadel, to the house of the women, into the charge of Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, and let their cosmetics be given them.

4The young woman who pleases the king, let her be queen in place of Vashti." This pleased the king, and he did so.

Mordecai and Esther

5There was a Jewish man in Susa the citadel whose name was Mordecai son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite,

6who had been carried into exile from Jerusalem with the exiles carried away with Jeconiah king of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had carried into exile.

7He was bringing up Hadassah, that is Esther, the daughter of his uncle, for she had neither father nor mother. The young woman was beautiful in form and lovely to look at, and when her father and mother died, Mordecai took her as his own daughter.

8When the king's word and his decree were proclaimed and many young women were gathered to Susa the citadel into the charge of Hegai, Esther also was taken to the king's house, into the charge of Hegai, keeper of the women.

9The young woman pleased him and won his kindness. He quickly gave her her cosmetics and her portions, and the seven young women chosen to be given her from the king's house, and he moved her and her young women to the best place in the house of the women.

10Esther had not made known her people or her kindred, for Mordecai had charged her not to make it known.

11Every day Mordecai walked back and forth in front of the court of the house of the women, to learn how Esther was and what was being done with her.

The Turn of Each Young Woman

12When each young woman's turn came to go in to King Ahasuerus, after twelve months under the rule for the women, for so the days of their beautifying were completed, six months with oil of myrrh and six months with spices and the cosmetics of the women,

13this was how the young woman went in to the king: whatever she asked for was given her to take with her from the house of the women to the king's house.

14In the evening she went in, and in the morning she returned to the second house of the women, into the charge of Shaashgaz the king's eunuch, keeper of the secondary wives. She did not go in to the king again unless the king delighted in her and she was called by name.

15When the turn came for Esther daughter of Abihail, the uncle of Mordecai, who had taken her as his own daughter, to go in to the king, she asked for nothing except what Hegai the king's eunuch, keeper of the women, advised. Esther won favor in the eyes of all who saw her.

Esther Made Queen

16Esther was taken to King Ahasuerus, into his royal house, in the tenth month, the month of Tebeth, in the seventh year of his reign.

17The king loved Esther more than all the women, and she won favor and kindness before him more than all the virgins. He set the royal crown on her head and made her queen in place of Vashti.

18Then the king gave a great feast for all his officials and servants, Esther's feast. He granted a release to the provinces and gave gifts, as befitted the king's bounty.

Mordecai Uncovers a Plot

19When the virgins were gathered a second time, Mordecai was sitting in the king's gate.

20Esther had not made known her kindred or her people, as Mordecai had charged her, for Esther did what Mordecai said, as she had when she was being brought up by him.

21In those days, while Mordecai was sitting in the king's gate, Bigthan and Teresh, two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the threshold, became angry and sought to lay a hand on King Ahasuerus.

22The matter became known to Mordecai, and he told Queen Esther, and Esther told the king in Mordecai's name.

23The matter was looked into and found to be so, and the two of them were hanged on a pole. It was written in the book of the chronicles before the king.

Notes

  • v5 "Mordecai son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish, a Benjaminite" — ish yemini. Kish is the name of Saul's father, a Benjaminite (1 Samuel 9:1), and Shimei the name of the man of the family of the house of Saul who cursed David as he fled (2 Samuel 16:5). The next chapter names Mordecai's enemy the Agagite (3:1).

  • v6 "carried into exile… the exiles carried away… had carried into exile" — galah four times in one verse. The exile with Jeconiah is the one told in 2 Kings 24:12–16.

  • v7 "Hadassah, that is Esther" — hadassah, from hadas, myrtle: instead of the brier shall come up the myrtle (Isaiah 55:13). The Greek says that when her parents died Mordecai brought her up for himself as a wife.

  • vv9, 17 "won his kindness… won favor and kindness before him" — va-tissa chesed, va-tissa chen va-chesed. Of Joseph in the round house: the LORD… extended kindness to him, and gave him favor in the eyes of the keeper (Genesis 39:21).

  • vv10, 20 "Esther had not made known her people or her kindred" — said twice, the second time with the reason: she did what Mordecai said. She makes it known at the second feast (7:4).

  • v14 "keeper of the secondary wives" — ha-pilagshim. A woman who had gone in to the king went to the second house, not back to the first.

  • v16 "in the tenth month… in the seventh year of his reign" — four years after the feast of 1:3. The Greek has the twelfth month, which is Adar.

  • v23 "hanged on a pole" — va-yittalu… al etz, on a tree or on wood, the word of the law: if you hang him on a tree, his body shall not remain all night on the tree (Deuteronomy 21:22–23). Haman has a pole made for Mordecai (5:14), and is hanged on it himself (7:10).

  • v23 "It was written in the book of the chronicles before the king" — the record that is read to the king on a sleepless night (6:1–2).

chapters.title: Haman's Decree
chapters.html:
Esther 3

Mordecai Will Not Bow

1After these things King Ahasuerus promoted Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite. He raised him up and set his seat above all the officials who were with him.

2All the king's servants who were in the king's gate bowed down and paid homage to Haman, for so the king had commanded concerning him. But Mordecai would not bow down or pay homage.

3Then the king's servants who were in the king's gate said to Mordecai, "Why are you transgressing the king's command?"

4When they had spoken to him day after day and he would not listen to them, they told Haman, to see whether Mordecai's words would stand, for he had told them that he was a Jew.

5When Haman saw that Mordecai did not bow down or pay homage to him, Haman was filled with wrath.

6But he scorned laying a hand on Mordecai alone, for they had told him who Mordecai's people were. So Haman sought to destroy all the Jews, the people of Mordecai, throughout the whole kingdom of Ahasuerus.

The Lot Is Cast

7In the first month, the month of Nisan, in the twelfth year of King Ahasuerus, they cast pur, that is, the lot, before Haman, from day to day and from month to month, to the twelfth month, the month of Adar.

8Then Haman said to King Ahasuerus, "There is a certain people scattered and kept apart among the peoples in all the provinces of your kingdom. Their laws are different from those of every other people, and they do not keep the king's laws, so it is not worth the king's while to let them be.

9If it pleases the king, let it be written that they be destroyed, and I will weigh out ten thousand talents of silver into the hands of those who do the work, to bring into the king's treasuries."

10So the king took his signet ring from his hand and gave it to Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite, the enemy of the Jews.

11The king said to Haman, "The silver is given to you, and the people also, to do with them as seems good to you."

The Letters Go Out

12Then the king's scribes were summoned on the thirteenth day of the first month, and it was written just as Haman commanded, to the king's satraps, to the governors over each province and to the officials of each people, to each province in its own script and to each people in its own language. It was written in the name of King Ahasuerus and sealed with the king's signet ring.

13Letters were sent by couriers to all the king's provinces, to destroy, to kill and to annihilate all the Jews, young and old, little children and women, in one day, the thirteenth of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to plunder their goods.

14A copy of the writing was to be given out as law in every province, published to all the peoples, so that they would be ready for that day.

15The couriers went out in haste at the king's word, and the law was given out in Susa the citadel. The king and Haman sat down to drink, but the city of Susa was thrown into confusion.

Notes

  • v1 "Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite" — Agag was the king of Amalek whom Saul spared against the word of the LORD, and whom Samuel put to death (1 Samuel 15:8–9, 32–33). Mordecai is of the line of Kish, Saul's father (2:5). After Amalek's attack in the wilderness Moses said, The LORD will have war with Amalek from generation to generation (Exodus 17:16). The Greek has Bougaios for the Agagite.

  • vv2, 5 "bowed down and paid homage… would not bow down or pay homage" — kor'im u-mishtachavim. The Hebrew does not say why Mordecai refused. It gives only what he told the servants: that he was a Jew (v4).

  • v4 "When they had spoken to him" — the read form, ke-omram. What is written is be-omram, a difference of one letter with the same sense.

  • v7 "they cast pur, that is, the lot" — pur, a word from outside Hebrew, explained by the Hebrew goral. The feast of Purim is named from it (9:24–26).

  • v8 "scattered and kept apart" — mefuzzar u-meforad: spread through every province, and separate from the peoples among whom they live.

  • v9 "ten thousand talents of silver" — Haman offers to pay for the killing himself. In v11 the king gives the silver back to him with the people.

  • v10 "his signet ring… the enemy of the Jews" — tsorer ha-Yehudim, Haman's title again at 8:1, 9:10 and 9:24. The ring is taken back from Haman and given to Mordecai (8:2).

  • v13 "to destroy, to kill and to annihilate" — le-hashmid la-harog u-le'abbed. Esther says the same three words to the king (7:4), and the king's second letter gives the Jews the right to do them to those who attack them (8:11). Here the Greek gives the text of the king's letter, which the English numbering places at 13:1–7.

  • v15 "the city of Susa was thrown into confusion" — navokhah. When Mordecai goes out in royal robes, the city of Susa shouted and rejoiced (8:15).

chapters.title: For a Time Like This
chapters.html:
Esther 4

Mourning among the Jews

1When Mordecai learned all that had been done, Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes. He went out into the city and cried out with a loud and bitter cry.

2He came as far as the front of the king's gate, for no one might enter the king's gate clothed in sackcloth.

3In every province, wherever the king's word and his law reached, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting and weeping and wailing; many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

Esther Learns of the Decree

4When Esther's young women and her eunuchs came and told her, the queen was deeply distressed. She sent clothes to clothe Mordecai, so that he would take his sackcloth off, but he would not accept them.

5Then Esther called Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs whom he had appointed to attend her, and ordered him to go to Mordecai to learn what this was and why it was.

6Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate.

7Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, and the exact sum of silver that Haman had promised to weigh out into the king's treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.

8He also gave him a copy of the written law that had been given out in Susa for their destruction, to show it to Esther and tell her, and to charge her to go in to the king to plead with him and to make request before him for her people.

9Hathach came and told Esther what Mordecai had said.

10Then Esther spoke to Hathach and gave him a message for Mordecai:

11"All the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that any man or woman who goes in to the king in the inner court without being called, there is one law for him: to be put to death, unless the king holds out to him the golden scepter, so that he may live. As for me, I have not been called to go in to the king these thirty days."

12They told Mordecai what Esther had said.

Mordecai's Answer

13Then Mordecai told them to answer Esther, "Do not imagine that in the king's house you alone of all the Jews will escape.

14For if you keep silent at this time, relief and deliverance will rise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father's house will perish. Who knows whether it is not for a time like this that you have come to the kingdom?"

15Then Esther told them to answer Mordecai,

16"Go, gather all the Jews who are found in Susa, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my young women will also fast in the same way. Then I will go in to the king, though it is against the law, and if I perish, I perish."

17Mordecai went away and did all that Esther had commanded him.

Notes

  • v1 "cried out with a loud and bitter cry" — va-yiz'aq ze'aqah gedolah u-marah, the words of Esau when he learned that Jacob had taken his blessing: he cried out with a great and exceedingly bitter cry (Genesis 27:34). Amalek, from whom Agag came, was Esau's grandson (Genesis 36:12).

  • vv3, 16 "fasting… fast for me" — the Hebrew names fasting, weeping and sackcloth, and no prayer. After v17 the Greek gives the prayers of Mordecai and of Esther, which the English numbering places at 13:8–14:19.

  • v7 "for the Jews" — the read form, ba-Yehudim. What is written, ba-Yehudiyyim, is a fuller spelling of the same word.

  • v11 "the golden scepter, so that he may live" — sharvit ha-zahav. The king holds it out to her in 5:2 and again in 8:4.

  • v14 "from another place" — mi-maqom acher. The Greek has from elsewhere. Mordecai does not say from where.

  • v14 "for a time like this" — le-et ka-zot; the same word, et, as at this time earlier in the verse.

  • v16 "if I perish, I perish" — ka'asher avadti avadti, the form of Jacob's words when he let Benjamin go down to Egypt: if I am bereaved, I am bereaved (Genesis 43:14).

  • v17 "did all that Esther had commanded him" — Esther had done what Mordecai commanded (2:10, 20). Here Mordecai does what she commands.

speech.text: Esther 4
Mourning among the Jews
When Mordecai learned all that had been done, Mordecai tore his clothes and put on sackcloth and ashes. He went out into the city and cried out with a loud and bitter cry.
He came as far as the front of the king's gate, for no one might enter the king's gate clothed in sackcloth.
In every province, wherever the king's word and his law reached, there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting and weeping and wailing; many lay in sackcloth and ashes.
Esther Learns of the Decree

When Esther's young women and her eunuchs came and told her, the queen was deeply distressed. She sent clothes to clothe Mordecai, so that he would take his sackcloth off, but he would not accept them.
Then Esther called Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs whom he had appointed to attend her, and ordered him to go to Mordecai to learn what this was and why it was.
Hathach went out to Mordecai in the city square in front of the king's gate.
Mordecai told him all that had happened to him, and the exact sum of silver that Haman had promised to weigh out into the king's treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.

He also gave him a copy of the written law that had been given out in Susa for their destruction, to show it to Esther and tell her, and to charge her to go in to the king to plead with him and to make request before him for her people.
Hathach came and told Esther what Mordecai had said.
Then Esther spoke to Hathach and gave him a message for Mordecai:

"All the king's servants and the people of the king's provinces know that any man or woman who goes in to the king in the inner court without being called, there is one law for him: to be put to death, unless the king holds out to him the golden scepter, so that he may live. As for me, I have not been called to go in to the king these thirty days."
They told Mordecai what Esther had said.
Mordecai's Answer
Then Mordecai told them to answer Esther, "Do not imagine that in the king's house you alone of all the Jews will escape.

For if you keep silent at this time, relief and deliverance will rise for the Jews from another place, but you and your father's house will perish. Who knows whether it is not for a time like this that you have come to the kingdom?"
Then Esther told them to answer Mordecai,

"Go, gather all the Jews who are found in Susa, and fast for me. Do not eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my young women will also fast in the same way. Then I will go in to the king, though it is against the law, and if I perish, I perish."
Mordecai went away and did all that Esther had commanded him.

chapters.title: Esther's First Feast
chapters.html:
Esther 5

Esther before the King

1And it came to pass on the third day that Esther put on her royal robes and stood in the inner court of the king's house, opposite the king's house. The king was sitting on his royal throne in the royal house, facing the entrance of the house.

2When the king saw Queen Esther standing in the court, she won favor in his eyes, and the king held out to Esther the golden scepter that was in his hand. Esther came near and touched the tip of the scepter.

3The king said to her, "What is it, Queen Esther? What is your request? Even to half of the kingdom, it shall be given you."

4Esther said, "If it pleases the king, let the king and Haman come today to the feast that I have prepared for him."

5Then the king said, "Bring Haman quickly, so that we may do as Esther has said." So the king and Haman came to the feast that Esther had prepared.

6As they drank wine at the feast, the king said to Esther, "What is your wish? It shall be granted you. What is your request? Even to half of the kingdom, it shall be done."

7Esther answered, "My wish and my request:

8if I have found favor in the eyes of the king, and if it pleases the king to grant my wish and to do my request, let the king and Haman come to the feast that I will prepare for them, and tomorrow I will do as the king has said."

Haman's Pride

9Haman went out that day glad and merry of heart. But when Haman saw Mordecai in the king's gate, and that he neither rose nor trembled before him, Haman was filled with wrath against Mordecai.

10Nevertheless Haman restrained himself and went home. He sent and brought his friends and Zeresh his wife,

11and Haman told them of the glory of his riches, the number of his sons, and all the ways the king had promoted him and how he had raised him above the officials and the king's servants.

12Haman said, "What is more, Queen Esther let no one but me come with the king to the feast she prepared. Tomorrow also I am invited by her, together with the king.

13Yet all this is worth nothing to me, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king's gate."

14Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends said to him, "Let a pole be made, fifty cubits high, and in the morning tell the king to have Mordecai hanged on it. Then go with the king to the feast, glad." The advice pleased Haman, and he had the pole made.

Notes

  • v1 "on the third day" — of the fast, three days, night or day (4:16). In the Greek, vv1–2 are a longer telling of Esther's coming before the king, which the English numbering places at 15:1–16.

  • v1 "put on her royal robes" — va-tilbash Ester malkhut, put on royalty. The word comes twice more in the verse: his royal throne, the royal house.

  • vv3, 6 "Even to half of the kingdom" — ad chatsi ha-malkhut, the king's promise three times (5:3, 6; 7:2). Herod makes the same promise to the daughter of Herodias: whatever you ask me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom (Mark 6:23).

  • v9 "he neither rose nor trembled before him" — lo qam ve-lo za'. In 3:2 he would not bow to Haman; now he does not even rise.

  • v10 "Haman restrained himself" — va-yit'appaq, Joseph's word before his brothers: he restrained himself and said, "Serve the bread" (Genesis 43:31), and Joseph could not restrain himself (45:1).

  • v11 "the number of his sons" — ten, named when they die (9:7–10).

  • v14 "a pole… fifty cubits high" — etz gavoah chamishim ammah, the etz of 2:23. The Greek also has wood of fifty cubits.
